stories.summary: Mike Vrabel's comments after the Patriots' loss to the Lions led to Mike Tomlin being about as honest as imaginable. Following the game, though, Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel gave a blunt breakdown, starting with, "Winners figure out ways to help the team win." Things got a bit more tense from there, as Vrabel didn't hold back much. When asked whether this Patriots group falls into that category, Vrabel backtracked slightly. "No, I mean, just in general. Dave Allan, 44, from Kenton, Newcastle, attempted the challenge on Saturday and made it to 80 miles, the equivalent of more than three consecutive marathons, before he had to stop. He said he was still happy to have run further than he ever had before, adding: "You won't find me offering any excuses, I just couldn't do it on the day, it was a bridge too far." Allan raised more than £4,300 for charity Gym Possible in Gateshead, which has specialist staff and equipment designed for people with disabilities.

stories.title: Ashes of exiled Nobel Laureate Miguel Ángel Asturias returned to Guatemala
stories.summary: The poet, writer and diplomat died in Europe in 1974 having been forced to leave his native country. The remains of writer and diplomat Miguel Ángel Asturias have been buried in his native Guatemala 52 years after he died in exile. His ashes were brought to Guatemala from Paris, where he had lived before his death from cancer in the Spanish capital, Madrid, in 1974. Asturias was awarded the Nobel Prize for Literature in 1967 for his vivid writings, which drew on the experiences of indigenous Guatemalans. The urn containing his ashes was placed in soil gathered from different parts of Guatemala at a cultural centre named after him in Guatemala City.
